note: Every fact checked on the NASA InSight mission page (challenge resource) and its science instruments page.

facts.text: InSight launched on 5 May 2018 on an Atlas V-401 from Vandenberg Air Force Base, California.
The rocket that launched InSight also launched two briefcase-sized CubeSats called Mars Cube One, or MarCO, which flew on their own path to Mars behind InSight.
InSight landed on 26 November 2018 on Elysium Planitia, a flat, smooth plain near Mars' equator, chosen for safety rather than for its surface features.
InSight studied the deep interior of Mars and was designed to take the planet's vital signs: its pulse, temperature and reflexes.
InSight was the first mission dedicated to investigating the deep interior of Mars. Its three main instruments were SEIS, HP3 and RISE.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: InSight science instruments (part of the challenge resource)

facts.text: SEIS, the seismometer, was a round, dome-shaped instrument that sat on the Martian surface under a domed Wind and Thermal Shield and waited for seismic waves from marsquakes and the thumps of meteorite impacts.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: InSight science instruments (part of the challenge resource)

facts.text: SEIS used up to 8.5 watts and returned 38 megabits of data per day.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: InSight science instruments (part of the challenge resource)

facts.text: InSight's sensors captured the low rumble of Martian wind, estimated at 5 to 7 metres a second, on 1 December 2018.

HP3, the heat probe, was designed to burrow almost 5 m into Mars to measure the heat flowing out of the planet. The arm placed it on the surface; its mole hammered itself in but met different soil than expected and could not reach the planned depth.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: InSight science instruments (part of the challenge resource)

facts.text: RISE tracked the lander's position precisely to measure how much Mars' north pole wobbles, revealing the size and composition of Mars' iron-rich core.
facts.sourceName: NASA Science: InSight science instruments (part of the challenge resource)
